title: Ce qui se passait et ce qui s'est passé
summary: Choose a past viewpoint: background, habit, completed event or interrupted activity.
objectives: Distinguish background and habitual situations from bounded past events.
Use être en train de in a past scene.
Interpret devoir without assuming that an obligation was necessarily fulfilled.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Ask what the sentence is doing
paragraphs: The imparfait opens a past scene: a description, an opinion at that time, an ongoing action or a habit. It does not show the beginning and end as a completed package. The passé composé reports a bounded event or interval and often moves a story forward. Duration alone does not choose the tense: a long job can be presented as completed, and a brief scene can be viewed in progress.

A habit often uses the imparfait, but a counted set of completed repetitions can use the passé composé. An account of events can use the passé composé without an imparfait. Conversely, a description can stay in the imparfait without an interruption.
points: Imparfait habit: je prenais ce bus chaque matin. Bounded repetition: j'ai pris ce bus trois fois hier.
An opinion can be background (je trouvais ce quartier agréable) or a reaction treated as a completed experience (j'ai trouvé la visite agréable). Neither tense is an automatic error with trouver.

examples.english: It was raining and the street was empty.

examples.french: Je **préparais** le repas quand le téléphone **a sonné**.
examples.english: I was preparing the meal when the telephone rang.

examples.french: Le dimanche, nous **rendions** visite à nos voisins.
examples.english: On Sundays, we used to visit our neighbours.

examples.french: Hier, nous **avons rendu** visite à trois voisins.
Je **trouvais** le travail intéressant, mais j'**ai changé** de poste.
examples.english: I found the work interesting, but I changed jobs.
examples.note: An opinion at the time contrasts with a completed change.

mistakes.why: Je elides before étais; the background tense itself is appropriate.

sections.title: Make an ongoing action or obligation explicit
paragraphs: Être en train de + infinitive highlights an action in progress at a reference moment. In the past use étais, étais, était, étions, étiez, étaient, followed by en train de and the infinitive. Je lisais often already means 'I was reading'; the longer expression adds emphasis, not a required English-style progressive.

Devoir in the imparfait gives the obligation, expectation or plan as background: je devais appeler does not establish whether I called. In the passé composé, j'ai dû appeler commonly reports a necessity that arose in the situation and often an action taken. It can also express an inference ('I must have called'); context decides. Do not equate every a dû with proof of fulfilment.
points: Devoir imparfait: je devais, tu devais, il/elle/on devait, nous devions, vous deviez, ils/elles devaient. Passé composé: j'ai dû, tu as dû, il/elle/on a dû, nous avons dû, vous avez dû, ils/elles ont dû.

examples.french: Nous **étions en train de charger** la voiture quand la pluie a commencé.
examples.english: We were loading the car when the rain started.
examples.note: The loading is explicitly in progress.

examples.english: I was supposed to call, but I forgot.

examples.french: Le pont était fermé ; nous **avons dû faire** un détour.
examples.english: The bridge was closed; we had to take a detour.
examples.note: A necessity arose during the journey.

mistakes.avoid: Elle était en train de préparait le dîner.
mistakes.prefer: Elle était en train de préparer le dîner.
mistakes.why: After en train de, use an infinitive, not a second conjugated verb.

practice.prompt: Describe the weather as background to an arrival.
choices: Il pleuvait quand elle est arrivée.
Il a plu quand elle arrivait.
answers: Il pleuvait quand elle est arrivée.
practice.explanation: The requested viewpoint makes rain background and arrival the event.

practice.prompt: Use the imparfait for a former habit: Chaque soir, nous ___ (lire) ensemble.
practice.explanation: A regular past activity uses the requested imparfait.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the imparfait: Vous ___ en train d'attendre.
Je devais envoyer le colis. Does this alone prove I sent it?
practice.explanation: An obligation does not establish its fulfilment.

practice.prompt: Use the imparfait for a description: La salle ___ (être) lumineuse.
practice.explanation: The sentence describes a past setting.

practice.prompt: Use the imparfait for an opinion at that time: Je ___ (trouver) ce quartier calme.
practice.explanation: The opinion is presented as background.

practice.prompt: Use the passé composé for the counted events: Hier, elle ___ (appeler) trois fois.
practice.explanation: The calls form a bounded set.

practice.prompt: Use the imparfait for the activity already underway: Nous ___ (dormir) quand l'alarme a sonné.
Complete with the infinitive: J'étais en train de ___ (écrire).
practice.explanation: Only être is conjugated in this expression.

practice.prompt: Use devoir in the imparfait for an unfulfilled plan: Ils ___ venir, mais ils ont annulé.
practice.explanation: The expected action did not happen.

practice.prompt: Use devoir in the passé composé: Le train était annulé ; nous ___ prendre un taxi.
practice.explanation: The context reports a necessity that arose.

practice.prompt: Can a completed-event account consist of J'ai appelé, j'ai réservé et j'ai payé?
practice.explanation: An event sequence does not need a background clause.

practice.prompt: Use the imparfait for a repeated childhood action: Enfant, je ___ (jouer) dehors après l'école.
Use the passé composé for a completed long interval: Nous ___ (travailler) dix heures, puis nous sommes rentrés.
practice.explanation: Long duration can still be bounded and completed.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the imparfait: Les agents ___ en train de vérifier les billets.
practice.explanation: Third-person plural être in the past.

practice.prompt: Which claim about elle a dû partir is accurate?
choices: It can express a necessity or an inference, depending on context.
It always proves that an obligation was fulfilled.
answers: It can express a necessity or an inference, depending on context.
practice.explanation: Devoir has more than one contextual reading.

production_task.prompt: Tell a friend about a small disruption during a journey. Set the scene, explain what was happening and say what you did next.
production_task.model_answer: Il neigeait et nous attendions le bus. Nous étions en train de consulter les horaires quand un agent a annoncé une annulation. Nous avons dû marcher jusqu'à une autre station. Le trajet a pris une heure.
production_task.translation: It was snowing and we were waiting for the bus. We were checking the timetable when an agent announced a cancellation. We had to walk to another station. The journey took an hour.
rubric: Use imparfait for the scene and activity in progress.
Use passé composé for the announcement and completed events.
Make the reason for the change clear.
